summary: Burst of 5xx errors during streaming shutdown propagation causing downstream runtime respawns and GPU warmup delays
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10 20:40 UTC Scriptly Inc reported a sustained spike in 5xx responses for streaming requests. The spike correlated with runtime worker restarts and delayed GPU warmup on a subset of Dedicated capacity nodes. Impact: customer streaming sessions experienced frequent disconnects and ~20-40% increased error rate for ~18 minutes. Several long-running streaming sessions were dropped and retried, amplifying downstream load. Environment: production, dedicated cluster serving Scriptly Inc tenant in us-east primary and failover in us-west.
timeline: 20:37 UTC - first customer report via support chat: multiple 502s on long-lived streams
20:39 UTC - automated alert: api-gateway 5xx rate > 15% for tenant Scriptly (threshold 5%)
20:41 UTC - SRE escalated, began attaching runtime and GPU-manager logs
20:45 UTC - temporary mitigation applied: scale up ephemeral worker pool (+50%) and increase accept-queue depth
20:55 UTC - error rate dropped back to baseline after autoscaler completed warmup and prefetch timeouts adjusted
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a long-lived streaming session against redwood/gpt-medium-v1 with sustained token output (avg response chunking every 200ms)
2) Trigger a graceful restart of serving-runtime on a subset (simulate rolling deploy) and attempt to resume streams
3) Observe keepalive/handshake failures and 5xx responses as clients attempt reconnection while GPU warmup is still ongoing
4) Note increased retry loops from client and higher prefetch cancellations leading to worker respawns
logs: [2026-03-10T20:40:12Z] apigw: upstream response status=502 tenant=scriptly request_id=abc123 streaming=true
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: rolling restart combined with prefetch cancellation caused a tight respawn loop on ephemeral workers which in turn delayed GPU warmup and caused apigw to surface 502s/503s
Correlated metrics: prefetch cancellation rate spiked from baseline 0.2% to 18% for affected tenant; worker restart rate climbed from 0.01/s to 0.6/s
Observed pattern: long-lived streaming clients reconnected repeatedly while runtime was still initializing model KV and GPU; apigw then hit upstream timeouts and returned 5xx
Reproducer confirmed in staging when inducing prefetch timeout = 50ms during concurrent worker restarts
No evidence of hardware failure on GPU hosts; warmup latency increased due to serialized prefetching and KV lock contention
customer_impact: Scriptly reported client-visible disconnects and a 35% reduction in successful streaming completions during the window
Attachments: customer provided sample request ids: abc123, def456, ghi789
Billing impact: elevated retries noted; potential overcharge concerns — flagged for finance review
comments: Asha Patel (Support): Received report from Scriptly support channel at 20:37 UTC — escalating to SRE.
Miguel Torres (SRE): Attaching runtime logs and increasing ephemeral pool while we investigate prefetch behavior. Temporary mitigation applied at 20:45 UTC.
Ivy Chen (Runtime): Found KV shard lock contention during concurrent prefetch cancellation; adding debug flags to runtime at 20:50 UTC for deeper traces.
Customer (Scriptly Ops): Confirmed stream stability improving after mitigation; requested root cause and timeline for a permanent fix.
Miguel Torres (SRE): Next steps - reduce serialized prefetch window, add faster fallback for long-lived streams, and update autoscaler cooldown to avoid repeated respawn cycles.
resolution: Mitigations applied: 1) Temporarily increased ephemeral worker pool to absorb reconnect storms; 2) raised prefetch abort timeout for affected tenant from 100ms -> 400ms to prevent immediate cancellation during warmup; 3) adjusted autoscaler cooldown to 120s to avoid churn. Result: 5xx rate returned to baseline within ~10 minutes. Current status: monitoring for recurrence; not yet a complete fix.
follow_up_actions: Schedule runtime change to serialize per-shard prefetches with backoff to avoid global warmup stalls (ENG-#),
Patch autoscaler to detect prefetch-induced respawn loops and temporarily increase warmup concurrency (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/334)
Add tenant-level prefetch telemetry to console dashboards and alerting for sustained prefetch cancellation >5%
Coordinate post-incident postmortem and customer-facing RCA within 72 hours
